review_scope: Read the complete current helper and inspected the existing-Sirach append path, exact native cohorts, historical preservation, source/check evidence construction, receipt binding, preparation manifest, maintenance capture, readback and guarded transaction code.

Verified the baseline proof against Git: 27 existing book records, 41 historical runs, 18446 completed sources and 23212 completed pairs. Existing Sirach has 1374 actual units in 52 native groups, with 199 completed objects, 20 deferrals and 8 candidates. The complete existing inventory and native prologue metadata remain unchanged.

Independently validated the actual Sirach 9-17 author packet at 225 native sources, 201 distinct passage pairs and 24 zero-credit deferrals. A clearly labelled synthetic peer receipt was used only inside scratch to exercise peer receipt guards; it is not semantic acceptance.

Independent scratch probes reject reordered or duplicated native cohorts, missing source dispositions, duplicated passage pairs, stale author/peer hashes, all four false author and peer reading flags, credited deferrals, unread candidates and hints falsely claiming reading or completion.

Independent object-audit probes reject changes to prior completed units, future unread units, native prologue metadata, prior deferral/candidate/source-pin/batch prefixes and prior runs. The positive fixture separately establishes that two distinct target passages on one new source count as two pairs and one source.

Read and accepted both clearly labelled technical preparation fixtures: zero supported pairs and two synthetic pairs. They preserve all 199 old completed objects, 20 deferrals, 8 candidates, 41 runs and 1374-unit inventory; the next 669 sources advance cumulative actual reading to 888 and next unread to Sirach 34:1, with no synthetic semantic credit.

Both full scratch fixtures passed the production validator for all 27 existing books, retaining historical archives in place. The current helper does not output inventory, editorial-note or renderer changes. The production renderer snapshot equals the exact baseline Git blob and the prior accepted renderer after newline normalization.

The safe-path, apply/rollback, receipt and publication-concurrency functions are AST-identical to the previously accepted helper. The code still journals before/after bytes, checks each write boundary, restores only its own after-bytes, preserves concurrent changes, and performs no recursive deletion. Focused contained-path probes were repeated; unrelated rollback tests were not repeated.

The readback exception for modified historical verses is restricted to this configured existing Sirach book; audit_objects then requires every unit outside the explicit cohort, every prior completed object and all native metadata to remain exact. Other books retain exact baseline verses/inventory/editorial records and their previous rendered Scripture.

Technical evidence archival validates contained relative paths and every listed hash, archives only explicitly referenced JSON results, and binds this receipt to the final helper. Preparation and publication remain separate; this technical acceptance provides zero source or pair completion credit.
